data.narrative:
OpenStar, a Seed-stage Climate & Energy company founded by Ratu Mataira and Thomas Berry, has raised $35M to date. The broader frontier-tech energy sector includes one public comparable (ticker: LNZA) and eight private peers spanning advanced materials, energy storage, and industrial decarbonization (including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen).

Two standard valuation approaches were assessed against available data. Stage-progression methodology was inapplicable: the implied $25.0B valuation derived from available funding-tracker proxies exceeds 20x the company's actual capital raised, indicating the base-value input was unreliable and warranting exclusion. Peer-median analysis was similarly not executable due to an insufficient comparable set—while nine same-sector peers exist, zero qualified at OpenStar's stage, adjacent stage, or comparable valuation tier. A broader cross-sector median would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity of frontier-energy business models and development timelines.

This analysis does not support a triangulated valuation range. The data constraints are acute: early-stage climate tech exhibits wide stage-to-valuation dispersion, peer financials remain largely opaque, and OpenStar's specific technical and commercial positioning relative to identified comparables cannot be quantified from available inputs. A credible valuation would require either comparable transaction multiples within a tightly filtered peer subset or forward-looking cash-flow assumptions specific to the company's technology and go-to-market timeline.
